transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I reluctantly agreed to come because my campus doctor insisted, but honestly, I feel like if I don’t keep really tight control over what I eat, I’ll gain weight and everything I’ve worked for will fall apart. I'm just terrified that if I let go of that control, my grades and my future career plans will completely slip away.
Do you believe you are overweight or too fat even when other people say you are thin, or is your strict eating mainly about staying in control and avoiding mistakes?

It’s really both. Even though people tell me I’ve gotten "so thin," when I look in the mirror I still see soft areas and feel like I need to lose more. At the same time, keeping strict control over my food is the only way I feel disciplined and in control of my life, which keeps everything I've worked for from falling apart.
Besides food and weight, do you also need things in your life to be excessively orderly, perfect, and under your control, or is this strictness mainly focused on your body shape and weight?

While the strictness is focused on food, it is deeply connected to my need to be perfect in my honors classes and my goal of becoming an art therapist. Managing my meals and keeping strict routines is the only way I can cope with the unpredictability of college life, shifting friend groups, and art critiques. I feel like if I lose control of my weight, my academic discipline and everything else I've worked for will completely fall apart.

If you were not worried about gaining weight or your body shape, would you still feel a strong need to restrict your eating just to feel in control or avoid mistakes? Which feels like the main reason you limit food: fear of being fat, or needing control and perfection?

It is really hard to separate the two because they feel completely tangled together. Restricting my food is how I cope with the unpredictability of college, but gaining weight feels like the ultimate sign of losing control and being lazy or a failure. Even if I didn't fear gaining weight, I would still crave that control, but right now, putting on weight feels like the exact moment where my success would completely fall apart.

When you are at a low weight, do you still genuinely believe you are too fat or that parts of your body are fat? Or do you mostly recognize that you are thin and restrict eating mainly to feel in control or avoid mistakes?

It’s definitely a mix of both. Even though my clothes are hanging off me and everyone says I'm thin, when I look in the mirror I still see soft areas and genuinely feel like I need to lose more weight. At the same time, keeping that tight control over what I eat is how I prove to myself that I'm disciplined and successful, and I feel like everything would fall apart if I let go of it.

Have you ever had times when you ate a large amount of food in a short time and felt out of control, or do you mainly just restrict your eating? Have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or exercised excessively to make up for eating?

No, I have never binged, made myself throw up, or used laxatives; for me, it is strictly about maintaining tight control and restricting. Most days I only have black coffee, half a granola bar, and a tiny salad, tracking everything on a spreadsheet to stay under my strict limit. The mere thought of eating normally, like pizza with my roommates, makes me feel incredibly panicky and out of control.
